content.answer: When updating an id-referenced single-select field, merge options by stable id — pass existing options through unchanged (names keep their old ids), and assign fresh ids only to genuinely new names, starting from max(existing id)+1; rebuilding the option list by name alone makes the API issue brand-new ids and silently clears the field value on every existing row.
content.reuse_advice: For any catalog/enum update where stored data references items by id (e.g., single-select, taxonomy, lookup tables), never replace the catalog wholesale based on display names. Always fetch the current catalog, diff by stable id, keep unchanged items byte-for-byte with their original ids, allocate new sequential ids only for additions (continuing from max(existing id)+1), and only then apply updates/deletions — otherwise every existing reference will be silently orphaned or cleared.
